overview: The committee discussed urban canopy preservation, transportation infrastructure improvements, and planning for the upcoming Circle the Square event. They also endorsed a previously contested electric vehicle charging station sign permit following clarifications from the applicant.

items.title: Administrative and Festival Updates
items.summary: Director Alicia Hunt reported on the extension of outdoor dining through 2023 and the hiring of interns to assist with the Harvest Heritage Festival in October.

items.title: Environmental Outreach and Events
items.summary: Members discussed educational activities for the June Circle the Square event and announced a rain barrel sale with pickup scheduled for May 11.

items.title: Tree and Urban Canopy Subcommittee Report
items.summary: Lauretta James recommended a temporary tree preservation ordinance to prevent clear-cutting while a permanent version is drafted and noted severe understaffing in the Forestry Department.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes of the March 7, 2022 meeting.

items.title: Solar Energy and Tree Canopy Integration
items.summary: Gaston Fiore proposed a 'solar exception' for tree ordinances to ensure urban canopy preservation does not hinder the installation of rooftop solar panels.

items.title: Transportation Subcommittee Overview
items.summary: Martha Ondras reviewed transit emissions, pedestrian safety projects, and the upcoming MBTA bus network redesign scheduled for public outreach in May.

items.title: Volta EV Charging Sign Permit
items.summary: Approved a motion to endorse the sign permit for electric vehicle charging stations at Stop & Shop after receiving clarification that the displays are static and partner-mandated.

items.title: Stretch Code and Net Zero Building Standards
items.summary: The committee discussed the state's draft net-zero building code, expressing concerns that the proposal lacks a clear definition of 'net zero' and is insufficiently strict for an opt-in standard.
